papers.title: Experimental Investigation of Gate-Switching Instability in SiC MOSFETs Under Mission-Profile-Related Non-Monotonic Stress
papers.summary: In high-power-density and efficient power electronic systems, SiC MOSFETs are increasingly used for their superior performance. However, their gate oxide/semiconductor interface remains challenging, and additional degradation mechanisms, such as gate-switching instability (GSI), occur. Extensive monotonic-stress studies have shown that negative gate-source voltage peaks dominate GSI-related degradation, even when occurring only during undershoots. Consequently, degradation depends on the mission profile because gate-voltage undershoot varies with gate resistance, gate-loop inductance, and drain current. However, the resulting non-monotonic GSI-related degradation has not been thoroughly investigated. This letter demonstrates that accounting for gate undershoots is crucial for estimating degradation over the component’s lifetime, as the pre-existing degradation level strongly influences further degradation. This behavior applies to both GSI-related defect activation and deactivation. Furthermore, defect deactivation is highly dependent on the positive gate-source voltage, and after a stress change, even 600 mV of degradation recovers to the degradation obtained under monotonic stress at the same gate-source voltage within ${2}\!\cdot\!{10}^{{11}}$ switching cycles. Additionally, GSI-related defect activation strongly depends on the degradation level, and consequently, mission-profile-related gate-voltage undershoots must be considered, even if they occur only during 5% of the mission profile.

papers.title: Ge/GeSn Quantum Well MOSFETs for Cryogenic Applications
papers.summary: Cryogenic CMOS provides critical performance benefits for high-performance computing, space electronics, and quantum interfaces due to enhanced carrier mobility and steeper subthreshold swing (SS). However, the band-tail effect limits the device performance at cryogenic temperatures. In this work, Ge/GeSn quantum well (QW) p-MOSFETs are studied from 300 K down to 5 K. Owing to the QW confinement and the presence of a Ge cap layer, interface-related band-tail states are significantly suppressed. As a result, the Ge/Ge 0.88 Sn 0.12 QW device exhibits a continuously decreasing SS, reaching 15 mV/dec at 5 K, which is the lowest reported SS among the Ge-based p-MOSFETs. This work highlights GeSn QW engineering as an effective strategy for cryogenic CMOS applications.

papers.title: 3-D Stacked 3T DRAM Cell Employing CFET With Depletion Mode PMOS
papers.summary: Conventional capacitor-less two-transistor dynamic random access memory (2T DRAM) suffers from storage node (SN) retention degradation and capacitive coupling, which induces read current variation and lowers computational accuracy. To address this, we propose a 3D stacked 3T DRAM cell featuring an In-Ga-Zn-O (IGZO) vertical channel transistor (VCT) as a write transistor and a Si complementary field effect transistor (CFET) read transistor composed of an enhancement mode NMOS and a depletion mode PMOS. The ultra-low leakage IGZO channel fundamentally improves retention. Simultaneously, the depletion mode PMOS compensates for read current reductions as SN voltage decreases. Simulations using Sentaurus TCAD and a customized framework verify that the proposed device stabilizes the read current and maintains CIFAR-10 inference accuracy degradation under 3 % for up to 8300 seconds, significantly outperforming prior works.

papers.title: High-Performance Polycrystalline InSnZnO Thin-Film Transistors and Their Inverters
papers.summary: High-performance polycrystalline InSnZnO (poly-ITZO) thin-film transistors (TFTs) are fabricated at low- temperature annealing conditions ( $350~^{\circ }$ C) via a novel Hafnium metal-induced crystallization (Hf-MIC) route, where ordered crystalline phase and suppressed oxygen defect play a critical role. The induced poly-ITZO TFTs show a high field-effect mobility ( $\mu _{\text {FE}}\text {)}$ of 80.1 cm 2 /V $\cdot $ s, and the threshold voltage shift ( $\Delta $ V ${}_{\text {TH}}\text {)}$ is only 0.05 V under positive bias temperature stress (PBTS) stability with an electric field of 2.5 MV/cm at $60~^{\circ }$ C for 3600 s. Notably, the poly-ITZO TFT achieves a trade-off between high mobility and excellent temperature stability. Owing to the superior electrical characteristics of poly-ITZO TFTs, a zero-V GS load inverter is built and achieves a high voltage gain of 1433 V/V at a supply voltage (V ${}_{\text {DD}}\text {)}$ of 10 V, which provides valuable insights for display scenarios and non-display applications of logic circuits.

papers.title: Impact of Drain Bias on Degradation of Amorphous-InGaZnO Thin-Film Transistors
papers.summary: In this work, the drain stress voltage ( $\mathrm{V}_{\mathbf {\text {DS}}}$ )-dependent reliability degradation behavior in amorphous indium-gallium-zinc-oxide (a-IGZO) thin-film transistors (TFTs) is investigated at a fixed positive gate stress voltage ( $\mathrm{V}_{\mathbf {\text {GS}}}$ ) of 30 V. As $\mathrm{V}_{\mathbf {\text {DS}}}$ increases from 0 to 5 V, the $\mathrm{V}_{\mathbf {\text {DS}}}$ -induced weakened vertical electric field alleviates positive threshold voltage shift ( $\Delta $ $\mathrm{V}_{\mathbf {\text {th}}}$ ), whereas a further increase in $\mathrm{V}_{\mathbf {\text {DS}}}$ toward 15 V accelerates degradation due to enhanced thermionic injection. The degradation results of the gate-to-source and gate-to-drain capacitance ( $\mathrm{C}_{\mathbf {\text {GS}}}$ and $\mathrm{C}_{\mathbf {\text {GD}}}$ ) under CCS at 5 V- $\mathrm{V}_{\mathbf {\text {DS}}}$ reveal suppressed electron trapping near the drain region due to the $\mathrm{V}_{\mathbf {\text {DS}}}$ -induced reduction in the vertical electric field. AC CCS measurements at 15 V- $\mathrm{V}_{\mathbf {\text {DS}}}$ show strong mitigation of $\Delta $ $\mathrm{V}_{\mathbf {\text {th}}}$ with decreasing stress duty ratio, confirming that SHE-induced thermionic injection becomes significant at high $\mathrm{V}_{\mathbf {\text {DS}}}$ . Notably, $\Delta $ $\mathrm{V}_{\mathbf {\text {th}}}$ under AC stress with a 5% duty ratio becomes smaller at 15 V- $\mathrm{V}_{\mathbf {\text {DS}}}$ than at 5 V- $\mathrm{V}_{\mathbf {\text {DS}}}$ confirming that the $\mathrm{V}_{\mathbf {\text {DS}}}$ -induced vertical electric field reduction becomes dominant when SHE is alleviated. Furthermore, the stress-time-divided technique employed to analyze the energy distribution of predominant trap sites demonstrates that thermionic injection promotes electron trapping into deeper states. In summary, the dominant degradation mechanism evolves with increasing $\mathrm{V}_{\mathbf {\text {DS}}}$ from degradation mitigation induced by vertical electric field reduction to enhanced deep-level electron trapping driven by SHE-induced thermionic injection.

papers.title: An Asynchronous Energy-Harvesting Pixel for CMOS Image Sensors
papers.summary: This letter presents an asynchronous energy-harvesting active pixel that provides a novel solution for self-powered image sensors. The proposed design employs a negative-voltage switch that automatically transitions the photodiode from imaging mode to energy-harvesting mode when the photodiode voltage drops below a threshold, without requiring synchronized timing control. By utilizing idle windows within the frame period, the pixel can achieve simultaneous imaging and energy harvesting within a single frame cycle. The prototype, fabricated in a standard 0.18- $\mu $ m CMOS process, operates at a 1 V supply with a frame rate of 35.9 fps, consuming a total power of $3.98~\mu $ W. It achieves a dynamic range of 45 dB, a pixel fill factor of 55.76%, and an energy-harvesting efficiency of 60.1 pW/lux/mm 2 while maintaining full imaging functionality.

papers.title: Dual-Mode TFT Synaptic Array for Energy-Efficient On-Chip Training
papers.summary: A dual-mode TFT synaptic array for on-chip training is proposed. The device employs an Al 2 O 3 /Si 3 N 4 /SiO 2 gate-insulator stack and supports low-voltage short-term (ST) and high-voltage long-term (LT) operation within the same platform. The ST mode shows gradual conductance modulation and negligible cycling degradation, whereas the LT mode provides a wider memory window and better retention. In the proposed training scheme, the LT region performs vector-matrix multiplication with stored weights, while the ST region accumulates low-voltage updates before threshold-triggered LT transfer. Hardware-aware simulation using the measured ST/LT characteristics yields a final MNIST test accuracy of 97.39%, versus 53.67% for direct LT-only updating, with a 59.7% reduction in LT high-voltage update events. These results indicate that the proposed same-device dual-mode TFT array is promising for energy-efficient on-chip training.

papers.title: Multi-Channel AlScN/GaN RF HEMTs Grown by Metal-Organic Chemical Vapor Deposition
papers.summary: We demonstrate multi-channel AlScN/GaN high electron mobility transistors (HEMTs) grown by metal-organic chemical vapor deposition (MOCVD). The five-channel structure exhibits a high electron mobility ( $\mu $ ) of 1030 cm 2 /V $\cdot $ s together with a high carrier concentration ( ${n} {_{\text {s}}}$ ) of ${3}.{58}\times {10} {^{{13}}}$ cm −2 . Devices with a gate length ( ${L} {_{\text {g}}}$ ) of 95 nm and a total gate width ( ${W} {_{\text {g}}}$ ) of ${2}\times {15}~\mu $ m were fabricated using a tri-gate architecture with varying fin widths. The 300 nm fin width device achieves a current density of 4.2 A/mm with improved linearity, while reducing the fin width to 75 nm enhances electrostatic control over all channels and yields ${f} {_{\text {T}}}$ / ${f} {_{\text {MAX}}}$ of 70/163 GHz. The passivated devices retain a stable I ${}_{\text {D,max}}$ under repeated measurements and an off-state breakdown of 18.5 V at ${\text L}_{\text {GD}} =400$ nm. These results highlight the promise of MOCVD-grown AlScN/GaN multi-channel HEMTs for RF applications, with strong DC and small-signal RF characteristics, motivating further study of their large-signal performance for mm-wave operation.
